correctness.rationale: Bounded self-adjoint summable commuting flips give an exact product Born law; each coordinate is Bernoulli with sin-squared parameter, supported on finite subsets. The mean is an improper Riemann-sum limit for a bounded-at-zero integrand with integrable power tail; gamma integration yields the displayed constant. The exact identity V(t)=mu(2t)/4 yields the variance/Fano limit. Bounded independent centered bits with diverging total variance satisfy Lindeberg and Berry--Esseen, while Chebyshev proves radial concentration. Exact assumptions alpha>1, c>0 and empty initial vertex are retained. The finite diagnostic script was run and passed; its output is not substituted for the analytical proof.

value.rationale: The 2026 source establishes dynamics on an unusual countable infinite-degree graph but lacks quantitative transport of the natural graph-radius observable. Summable power-law edge strengths are a motivated scale-free family. The theorem identifies its exact nontrivial t^(1/alpha) spreading exponent, explicit gamma amplitude, strictly sub-Poisson limiting Fano constant, Gaussian fluctuations and quantitative convergence rate. These characterize typical propagation and fluctuations beyond spectral/time-reversal results or a finite-time product identity; not an arbitrary numerical slice.
